title: Sampling Informer Proxy: aggregate low-cost sampling hints out of tracer hotpath
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a small, low-allocation component called the Sampling Informer Proxy that moves the work of producing sampling decisions off the tracer hotpath. The proxy will aggregate lightweight hints from background telemetry and recent decisions, synthesize compact rate-limited sampling weights per route/model/tenant, and expose them to the tracer hotpath via a lock-free, read-optimized shared memory path.

Why this work matters:
- Current tracer hotpath performs several allocations and map lookups to decide sampling for high-QPS routes. This contributes measurable p99 latency and CPU under load.
- Existing approaches (full prefiltering, background commit) either still touch hotpath or have coarse granularity. We want a middle ground: nearly zero-cost reads on the hotpath with near-real-time adaptive decisions.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Reduce tracer hotpath allocations by >= 60% under representative 95th/99th-percentile load in our perf harness.
- Maintain effective trace coverage for high-error/latency routes: end-to-end sampled errors must remain within 2% of baseline sampling coverage for error-producing requests.
- Keep decision staleness below configurable window (default 10s) and allow operator to tune to 30s for very high throughput.
- No increase in end-to-end 99th request latency beyond measurement noise caused by sampling change (<1%).

Design overview:
1) Informer Proxy: a small service (can run as sidecar or colocated daemon) that consumes micro-hints published by downstream services and background collectors. Hints are tiny structs: {route_key, tenant, hint_score, ttl} and are append-only.
2) Aggregation & Rate-limiting: proxy aggregates hints into compact sampling weights per key using exponential moving average + decay. It applies a global rate limiter to avoid thrashing when many keys spike.
3) Expose read path: the proxy exposes a lock-free read handle implemented as a memory-mapped, fixed-size ring of records or a packed byte buffer with sequence counters (compare-and-swap free readers). The tracer hotpath reads a small fixed-size entry by index computed from hash(key) and uses the packed byte (1-2 bytes) as the sampling weight.
4) Hotpath fallback: if the read entry is stale or absent, default to the existing lightweight probabilistic sampler.
5) Safety: updates to shared memory are atomic and happen at low frequency (configurable; default 1s). Proxy validates inputs and rate-limits expensive aggregates.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Prototype (2 weeks): implement a standalone informer proxy binary and a tiny C-compatible shared memory format; add a tracer read shim that reads the shared buffer and falls back on the old path. Run the perf harness on a single service.
B) Hardening (2 weeks): add aggregation decay tuning, backpressure when proxy is overloaded, and telemetry for hint ingestion rate, write latency, read miss rate.
C) Canary rollout (2 weeks): enable on select high-QPS services with canary sampling toggles; compare allocation/latency and sampling coverage.
D) Global rollout & docs (1 week): add operator config (stale_window, update_interval, buffer_size), runtime flags, and a console dashboard for sampling_hint_update_rate and effective_sample_rate per route.

Telemetry & dashboards to add:
- sampling_informer_hint_ingest_rate (per route/tenant)
- sampling_informer_agg_rate (how many keys updated/sec)
- sampling_informer_hotpath_read_miss_rate (per service)
- tracer_hotpath_alloc_bytes (before/after)
- sampled_spans_per_1k_requests (compare baseline vs informer on canary)
- sampling_decision_staleness_seconds (histogram)

Acceptance tests and perf validation:
- Unit tests for buffer read/write semantics and staleness detection.
- Integration test: enable informer in a staging cluster and replay production traffic for 1 hour; assert allocations drop >= 60% and sampled error coverage within 2% of baseline.
- Chaos test: kill proxy process mid-run to verify graceful fallback and no tracer crashes.

Rollout plan & guardrails:
- Start with rate-limited canary on 3 services (non-critical infra). If acceptance metrics are good, expand to top-10 QPS services.
- Add automatic rollback if tracer_hotpath_alloc_bytes does not improve by expected margin or if sampled_spans_per_1k_requests drops > 5% on error routes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Memory map vs in-process lockless structure: mmap cross-process gives isolation but adds operational surface; in-process shared ring is faster but requires sidecar co-scheduling. We'll prototype with mmap for broader compatibility.
- How many bits for weight: 8-bit packed weight gives compactness; we need quantization experiments.
- Backpressure policy when too many keys update: drop least-recently-updated keys vs global decay. We'll start with LRU+decay.

Links / artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood/obs/sampling-informer-proxy (placeholder)
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood/perf-harness/pull/412 (placeholder)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood/tracing/pull/999 (placeholder)

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on whether the read path is sufficiently cheap for a tight hotpath and whether the staleness window is configurable enough for different SLOs.
- The implementation should avoid any heap allocation in the fast read path and keep the read to a single atomic read + small bit ops.

If this ticket looks good I will split follow-ups for (1) mmap vs sidecar trade study, (2) per-tenant memory budgeting, (3) console visualization for heatmap of sampling weights.
